title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own writing. It is a typed English page, scanned upside down and hand-numbered 352 in the archive, carrying the section title "Non-Abelian periods on smooth manifolds". Its content, notation (model, ρ-images of model generators, the nilpotent quotients Γ_k of π_1, the footnote crediting Chen) and wording match Dennis Sullivan's work on minimal models, "Infinitesimal computations in topology" (Publ. Math. IHÉS 47, 1977). It is most likely a page of a preprint or typescript of that paper, circulating at IHÉS around 1975–76; the same section and example appear there. Grothendieck probably used the blank side for his notes, which explains the inversion.

The mathematics, in modern terms:
- Take a Sullivan minimal model (ΛV, d) of a smooth manifold M, with a quasi-isomorphism ρ into the de Rham algebra.
- The degree-1 generators and their differentials (the "d-formulae") determine a tower of nilpotent Lie algebras dual to the Malcev completions of the quotients π_1/Γ_k.
- Integrating the ρ-images of the generators along loops, corrected by iterated integrals, gives a complete set of "non-abelian periods". These are coordinates on the unipotent (Malcev) completion of π_1.

The example is the Heisenberg stage of such a model:
- The model begins Λ(x_1, x_2, y) with dy = x_1x_2.
- The corresponding forms satisfy dω_i = 0 and dη = ω_1∧ω_2.
- For a loop γ based at p, the periods are ∫_γω_1, ∫_γω_2 and ∫_γη − ∫_γ(∫_{γ_t}ω_1)ω_2.
- The third is a Chen iterated integral ∫η − ∫ω_1ω_2. It is homotopy invariant (rel basepoint) because the defect of the iterated integral under homotopy is cancelled by dη = ω_1∧ω_2. This is a Massey-product-type period.
- Under concatenation the triple (x, y, z) composes like upper unitriangular 3×3 matrices. This gives a homomorphism from π_1(M, p) to the real Heisenberg group, which factors through the 3-step quotient π_1/Γ_3 ⊗ ℝ.
- The footnote credits Chen for iterated integrals in general and claims the model theory guides their efficient use in homotopy theory.

In the archive context the page sits between Grothendieck's handwritten pages on a resolution C^* of k with Z^i ≅ Λ^i (previous page) and on maps Z^{i+1}⊗Z^j → Z^{i+j+1} and decompositions of Λ^{i+j+1} (next page). This suggests he was studying Sullivan-style multiplicative resolutions while preparing his 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex.
errors: Sign convention: with the minus sign in z = ∫η − ∫(∫ω_1)ω_2 and dη = ω_1∧ω_2, concatenation gives z(γ_1γ_2) = z_1 + z_2 − x_1y_2, not +x_1y_2 as the displayed matrix product gives. Up to replacing z by −z, or changing the orientation/sign convention of the iterated integral, the statement is correct. The overall sign also depends on the convention for which form is integrated first in Chen's iterated integral.
Homotopy invariance holds for homotopies rel basepoint. The third period depends on the choice of η, which is defined only up to a closed form; this is implicit and harmless.

ideas.what: Periods of loops from a minimal model: integrating ρ-images of degree-1 generators, plus iterated-integral corrections, gives a determining set of invariants of the nilpotent quotients of π_1.
ideas.modern_name: Unipotent/Malcev completion of π_1 via Sullivan 1-minimal model; Chen's π_1 de Rham theorem
ideas.usually_credited_to: K.-T. Chen (iterated integrals, 1970s); D. Sullivan (Infinitesimal computations in topology, 1977)
ideas.where_published: Sullivan, Publ. Math. IHÉS 47 (1977), section on non-abelian periods; Chen, Bull. AMS 1977 'Iterated path integrals'

ideas.what: Heisenberg example: dη = ω_1∧ω_2 makes ∫η − ∫ω_1ω_2 a homotopy invariant, and periods compose like unitriangular 3×3 matrices.
ideas.modern_name: Iterated-integral representation of Massey products / Heisenberg representation of π_1

missed.claim: Archival/historical fact: a typescript page of Sullivan's rational-homotopy/minimal-model paper is physically inside Grothendieck's 1975–76 notes for his IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex. The handwritten pages around it treat multiplicative resolutions with Z^i ≅ Λ^i. This documents that Grothendieck was reading Sullivan's de Rham-model approach to homotopy while thinking about a divided-power (integral/char p) de Rham complex, an early precursor of integral or p-adic analogues of Sullivan models. The mathematics on this page is Sullivan's, not Grothendieck's.
missed.quote: These iterated integrals have been considered in a general way, by Chen. Our theory seems to guide their efficient application to homotopy theory.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical link between Sullivan's rational homotopy theory and Grothendieck's divided-power de Rham thinking, before 'Pursuing Stacks' and his later remarks on schematic homotopy types. It is of mild interest for histories of integral and p-adic homotopy theory (Cartan divided powers, Mandell's p-adic E∞ models, Toën's affine stacks).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a known published text (Sullivan 1977), not Grothendieck's mathematics. Its only interest is historical: it shows Grothendieck engaging with Sullivan's models in the context of divided-power de Rham complexes around 1976.
transcription_corrections: The page is scanned upside down; it is a typed English text, likely from Sullivan's preprint, not Grothendieck's handwriting.
'ingegrals' is a genuine typo in the original typescript, not a transcription error.
The footnote marker '1' is attached to the third integral; ∫_{γ_t} denotes integration over the initial segment of γ up to time t.
